question: One patient is diagnosed with a 4 cm lung cancer without pleural contact in the right upper lobe. The extension study reveals the presence of metastasis in right parahilar nodes, without evidence of distant metastasis. The staging of the tumor will be:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "4 cm lung cancer" -> "no pleural contact" -> "metastasis in right parahilar nodes" -> "no distant metastasis" -> "staging indicates regional spread" -> "classified as Stage IIIA" -> 85%

CHAIN: "4 cm lung cancer" -> "right upper lobe location" -> "presence of parahilar node metastasis" -> "no distant metastasis" -> "staging suggests advanced local disease" -> "likely Stage IIIA" -> 80%
CHAIN: "4 cm lung cancer" -> "size and location noted" -> "metastasis to regional lymph nodes" -> "absence of distant spread" -> "indicates Stage IIIA" -> 90%
CHAIN: "4 cm lung cancer" -> "4 cm size" -> "regional lymph node involvement" -> "no distant metastasis" -> "consistent with Stage IIIA" -> 88%
analysis: The patient has a 4 cm lung cancer in the right upper lobe with metastasis to the right parahilar nodes. According to the AJCC staging system, this would classify as Stage IIB, as it involves regional lymph nodes (N1) but no distant metastasis (M0).
